title: Cap. VIII: First and proximate causes — inhering corruption reigns
pass_a_gloss: Therefore Adam's fall is death's reign's first cause, while the proximate cause is the sin that fall produced and that now inheres in everyone. Because that inhering sin reigns, death reigns too. Placeus presses the description: the sin in people not merely exists but lives; not merely lives but reigns; people serve it, obey it, and carry its law in their members. That reigning thing is not Adam's own actual sin; it is the effect of Adam's actual sin — namely inhering corruption. This closes the reply to the verse-17 argument.
pass_b_english: So Adam's fall is the first cause of death's reign, but the proximate cause is the sin produced from it and inhering in all; and because that sin reigns, death also reigns. Certainly the sin in human beings not only is, but lives; not only lives but reigns — the sin they serve, the sin they obey, whose law is in their members. That is not Adam's actual sin, but its effect: inhering corruption.
source_text: Est igitur lapsus Adae prima causa regni mortis, sed proxima est ab illo productum peccatum omnibus inhaerens, quod quia regnat, etiam mors regnat. Certe peccatum quod in hominibus non modo est, sed vivit; non modo vivit sed regnat; cui serviunt, cui obediunt, cujus lex est in membris. Id non est peccatum actuale Adami, sed hujus effectum, corruptio inhaerens.
